newsitem.title: JAPAN: North Korea says mourning over, Kim still no title.
newsitem.headline: North Korea says mourning over, Kim still no title.

text.p: North Korea said on Tuesday the official mourning period for its late president Kim Il-sung was over, signalling the start of a new stage in the communist nation's political development.

However, official North Korean media reports on a national memorial service held on Tuesday to commemorate the third anniversary of Kim's death made no mention of his son Kim Jong-il taking on the formal titles of party chief and state president.

"We solemnly re-state our heartful pledge to our father the great leader (Kim Il-sung) at this important occasion when the mourning is over," Foreign Minister and Vice Premier Kim Yong-nam told the memorial service, the official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said in a report monitored in Tokyo.

Kim Il-sung died on July 8, 1994, and his eldest son and heir Kim Jong-il, although in undisputed control of the country, has yet to be named general-secretary of the ruling Korean Worker's (communist) Party or state president.
In his address, Kim Yong-nam said there was no question over the succession itself but used only the "great leader" title when referring to Kim Jong-il.
Kim Jong-il was at the memorial service in the North Korean capital Pyongyang but had so far not given any speech.
